title: The library desk, from the business side
subtitle: Northgate Public Library on the crm engine

slides.heading: The library desk
slides.narration: This is the business view of the library domain. One minute shows how a loan request becomes a decision, a sign-off, and a loan on the shelf.

slides.heading: What the desk receives
slides.narration: The desk works a queue of loan requests. Each request names one title, the copy counts, and the price. The borrower's membership and its loan count sit beside it.

slides.heading: The rules that decide
slides.narration: Three rules carry the business. A checkout needs one free copy. Every loan runs fourteen days. A borrower holds at most three loans at the same time, on both membership tiers.

slides.heading: The agent at the desk
slides.narration: The case agent works each request the way a librarian would. It reads the loan rules and the manual, and approves, declines, or refers. The scoreboard scores every run against the workers' own decisions.

slides.heading: The lead's sign-off
bullets: A term over fourteen days waits
The lead librarian signs it off
Then the system issues the loan
slides.narration: Longer terms never issue themselves. A loan over fourteen days waits for the lead librarian's sign-off, and the system issues the loan only after it.

slides.heading: What the business sees
slides.narration: The business gets a queue that clears itself, a decision with its reason on every request, and a score that the improvement loop keeps raising.
